title: Colimits, mapping spaces and compact objects in homotopy pullbacks
statement:
Use the infinity-category and universe conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], and the filteredness, compactness and local smallness conventions of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal C$ and $G:\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$ be functors of infinity categories, and let $\mathcal P=\mathcal A\times^h_{\mathcal C}\mathcal B$. The homotopy pullback means the pullback of infinity categories, retaining coherent equivalences between the two images. It can be modeled by the simplicial pullback $(\mathcal A\times\mathcal B)\times_{\mathcal C\times\mathcal C}\operatorname{Eq}(\mathcal C)$, where $\operatorname{Eq}(\mathcal C)$ is the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal C)$ on equivalence edges, with its two endpoint projections. Objects of $\mathcal P$ are triples $(a,b,e)$ with $e:F(a)\simeq G(b)$. For $x=(a,b,e)$ and $y=(a',b',e')$ there is a natural equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P}(x,y)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal A}(a,a')\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(F(a),G(b'))}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(b,b'),$$
where the two maps send $u$ to $e'\circ F(u)$ and $v$ to $G(v)\circ e$. In particular, if the three categories are locally small (their mapping spaces are small), so is $\mathcal P$.

For every small simplicial set $K$, if $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ admit $K$-indexed colimits and $F,G$ preserve them, then $\mathcal P$ admits them. A cocone in $\mathcal P$ is a colimit cocone if and only if both its component cocones are colimit cocones. For any infinite regular cardinal $\lambda$ such that $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ admit small $\lambda$-filtered colimits preserved by $F,G$, a triple $(a,b,e)$ is $\lambda$-compact in $\mathcal P$ whenever $a,b,F(a)\simeq G(b)$ are $\lambda$-compact in $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal C$, respectively.

Write $\mathcal E_{/z}$ for the coherent slice of arrows into $z$, whose morphisms are commuting triangles with their specified homotopies and higher compatibilities. The same pullback description holds for slices: for every $x=(a,b,e)$, $\mathcal P_{/x}\simeq\mathcal A_{/a}\times^h_{\mathcal C_{/F(a)}}\mathcal B_{/b}$, where $e$ identifies $\mathcal C_{/G(b)}$ with $\mathcal C_{/F(a)}$. Restricting the three source categories to full subcategories compatible with $F,G$ restricts this equivalence to the corresponding full subcategory of triples. Slices have small mapping spaces when their ambient categories do. Moreover, let $\mathcal A'\subseteq\mathcal A$, $\mathcal B'\subseteq\mathcal B$ and $\mathcal C'\subseteq\mathcal C$ be full subcategories with $F(\mathcal A')\subseteq\mathcal C'$ and $G(\mathcal B')\subseteq\mathcal C'$, and let $\mathcal P'\subseteq\mathcal P$ be the full subcategory of triples $(a,b,e)$ with $a\in\mathcal A'$ and $b\in\mathcal B'$. Then $\mathcal P'$ is the homotopy pullback $\mathcal A'\times^h_{\mathcal C'}\mathcal B'$ of the restricted functors. If $\mathcal A',\mathcal B',\mathcal C'$ are essentially small, meaning each is equivalent to a small quasicategory, then $\mathcal P'$ is essentially small.

source.place: Lemmas 5.4.5.4, 5.4.5.5 and 5.4.5.7; mapping spaces of a homotopy fiber product as used in their proofs Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: Put $E=\operatorname{Eq}(\mathcal C)$. The endpoint map $q:\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal C)\to\mathcal C\times\mathcal C$ is an isofibration by [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation], using $\partial\Delta^1\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$. Its restriction to $E$ is still an isofibration. For an inner-horn lifting problem the filler has only the already specified vertices, so remains in this full subcategory. For an equivalence-lifting problem, the lift in the arrow category is an equivalence square; its two endpoint maps are equivalences by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. If its source arrow is an equivalence, its target arrow is also an equivalence, since the square identifies the latter with a composite of three equivalences. Thus the lifted vertex remains in $E$. This proves the asserted restriction property, rather than assuming that every full-subcategory restriction is an isofibration.

source.place: Agent expansion of the categorical-fibration model used in Lemmas 5.4.5.2-5.4.5.7; Kerodon 033R and exponential corner-map theorem 01F1

proof.text: The constant-arrow functor $s:\mathcal C\to E$ is an equivalence inverse to $\operatorname{ev}_0$: $\operatorname{ev}_0s=1$, and the transformation $s\operatorname{ev}_0\to1_E$ has at $e:c\simeq d$ the square $(1_c,e)$. It is coherent: on an arrow parameter $t$ and a transformation parameter $r$ it is induced by the monotone map $(t,r)\mapsto\min(t,r)$ on $[1]\times[1]$. Its components are equivalences by the same pointwise criterion. The two endpoint functors on $E$ are identified by the universal equivalence $e$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-pullback-limit] to $q|_E$ and $(F,G):\mathcal A\times\mathcal B\to\mathcal C\times\mathcal C$. Its strict pullback $P_0$ is a quasicategory and represents the claimed homotopy pullback: replacing the diagonal $\mathcal C\to\mathcal C\times\mathcal C$ by the equivalent object $E$ replaces equality of images by their coherent equivalence. We work with $P_0$ henceforth. All categories can be regarded as small in a larger universe for this application; the original meaning of small in the conclusions is unchanged.

source.place: Agent expansion of the categorical-fibration model used in Lemmas 5.4.5.2-5.4.5.7; Kerodon 033R and exponential corner-map theorem 01F1

proof.text: Compute first with the unpinched arrow spaces $U_D(z,w)=\{z\}\times_D\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,D)\times_D\{w\}$ of [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison]. Internal functor simplicial sets and fixed-endpoint fibers commute with strict pullbacks: in degree $n$ a map from $\Delta^n\times\Delta^1$ into a pullback is exactly a pair of maps with equal composites. Thus $U_{P_0}(x,y)$ is the strict pullback of $U_{\mathcal A}(a,a')\times U_{\mathcal B}(b,b')$ and $U_E(e,e')$ over $U_{\mathcal C}(F(a),F(a'))\times U_{\mathcal C}(G(b),G(b'))$. The second leg is a Kan fibration by the last assertion of [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation], applied to the inner fibration $E\to\mathcal C\times\mathcal C$. This is therefore a homotopy pullback by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. The natural pinch equivalences replace all $U$ spaces by the stated mapping spaces: their naturality gives strictly commuting comparison cospans, so [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance] applies. Fullness of $E$ identifies its mapping space with that in the arrow category. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-arrow-morphism-square] to $e$ and $e'$, including its compatibility with the joint endpoint map. Substitution into the preceding pullback cancels the two endpoint factors by the pasting and cancellation assertions of [lem-coef-infinity-homotopy-pullback-pasting]. What remains is precisely the space of $u:a\to a'$, $v:b\to b'$ and a path $e'F(u)\simeq G(v)e$, with all higher simplices. This is the displayed formula in the statement, naturally in $x,y$. If all three categories are locally small, choose small Kan models for the three mapping spaces; their path-space pullback is small degree by degree, so $\mathcal P$ is locally small.

source.place: Mapping-space argument in Lemma 5.4.5.2; arrow-square description in Kerodon Theorem 8.3.7.1 (06BZ)

proof.text: The same model works for diagrams. For any small simplicial set $T$, a map $T\times\Delta^n\to P_0$ is the pair of component diagrams and a transformation between their images whose vertex arrows are equivalences. By [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] this is exactly an equivalence in $\operatorname{Fun}(T,\mathcal C)$. Permuting the $T$ and $\Delta^1$ parameters therefore identifies $\operatorname{Fun}(T,P_0)$ with the equivalence-arrow pullback model for the functor categories. This is compatible with restriction in $T$, in particular with the constant-diagram functors.

source.place: Lemma 5.4.5.5, existence of a componentwise colimit cocone; coherent choices expanded by the partial universal-arrow criterion

proof.text: Now let $d:K\to\mathcal P$ have component diagrams $a_K,b_K$ and equivalence $e_K:Fa_K\simeq Gb_K$. Choose component colimits $a_\infty,b_\infty$. Their image cocones are colimiting by the preservation hypotheses. There is a coherent equivalence $e_\infty:F(a_\infty)\simeq G(b_\infty)$ identifying these cocones along $e_K$. To justify this coherence, apply the opposite assertion of [lem-coef-parametric-universal-arrows] to $\Delta_K:\mathcal C\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)$, restricted on the diagram side to the full subcategory of diagrams admitting colimits. The dual cone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] supplies its universal arrows. The resulting partial colimit functor $L$ and its coherent unit give an equivalence $L(Fa_K)\simeq L(Gb_K)$ and a square identifying its two universal cocones along $e_K$. The chosen image cocones with apices $F(a_\infty)$ and $G(b_\infty)$ are also initial in their respective cocone categories. By the contractibility assertion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], each is coherently equivalent, as a cocone, to the corresponding universal cocone supplied by $L$. Composing these two cocone equivalences with the square for $L(e_K)$ gives $e_\infty$ and its compatibility with the chosen image cocones. Only diagrams in the full subcategory admitting colimits are used; no other diagram in $\mathcal C$ is asserted to have a colimit. The diagram-model identification in step 4 then gives a cocone on $d$ with apex $(a_\infty,b_\infty,e_\infty)$.

source.place: Lemma 5.4.5.5, existence of a componentwise colimit cocone; coherent choices expanded by the partial universal-arrow criterion

proof.text:
For any test triple $y=(a',b',e')$, apply step 3 to the apex constructed in step 5. Contravariant representables take the three colimits $a_\infty,b_\infty,F(a_\infty)$ to limits by [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits]. Hence
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P}((a_\infty,b_\infty,e_\infty),y)\simeq\lim_{k\in K^{\mathrm{op}}}\bigl(\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal A}(a_k,a')\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(F(a_k),G(b'))}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(b_k,b')\bigr)\simeq\lim_{k\in K^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P}(d_k,y).$$
Here interchanging the limit with the pullback is just the limit universal property: a map into either expression is a family of maps into the two outer diagrams together with the same coherent identification of their maps into the middle diagram. The functor-category pointwise limit assertion of the cited node ensures these are coherent diagrams of spaces; one may enlarge the space universe for this calculation if the original categories are not locally small. The equivalences are the ones induced by the constructed cocone, because $e_\infty$ was chosen with its cocone compatibility. The dual mapping-space criterion of the cited node proves the cocone colimiting. The same calculation proves that every cocone whose two components are colimiting is colimiting. Conversely compare any colimiting cocone with the constructed one: both are initial in the cocone category, so their comparison is an equivalence by the contractibility assertion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Its projections are equivalences of component cocones. Their mapping-space universal properties are consequently the same, so both component cocones are colimiting. This proves existence and the two-way characterization, including $K=\varnothing$.

source.place: Lemma 5.4.5.5, both directions of the colimit criterion, proved using mapping spaces

proof.text:
Fix $x=(a,b,e)$ with the three compactness hypotheses and a small $\lambda$-filtered diagram $d:I\to\mathcal P$. Steps 5-6 construct its colimit $d_\infty$ componentwise. Put $A_i=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal A}(a,a_i)$, $B_i=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(b,b_i)$ and $C_i=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(F(a),G(b_i))$. Step 3 gives $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P}(x,d_i)\simeq A_i\times^h_{C_i}B_i$ naturally in $i$. The cospan simplicial set has three vertices and two nondegenerate edges, so is $\lambda$-small even for $\lambda=\aleph_0$. Apply [lem-coef-spaces-kappa-limit-filtered-colimit] to this shape and $I$:
$$\operatorname{colim}_I\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P}(x,d_i)\simeq(\operatorname{colim}_I A_i)\times^h_{\operatorname{colim}_I C_i}(\operatorname{colim}_I B_i)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P}(x,d_\infty).$$
The second equivalence uses that the compactness definition in [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category] makes the three image cocones for $a$, $b$ and $F(a)$ colimiting in the relevant space universe, together with preservation of the component colimit by $G$ for the $C_i$ term. The equivalent object $G(b)$ has the same compactness property by precomposition with $e$. Applying the finite-limit interchange to these three colimiting cocones gives the displayed colimit of the homotopy pullback. If mapping spaces are considered in a larger universe, the same argument applies there; a $\lambda$-small diagram into $I$ has only $<\lambda$ simplices, so filteredness is unchanged by enlargement. Naturality in step 3 identifies the resulting equivalence with the compactness comparison for $x$, so this is exactly $\lambda$-compactness under the stated definition.

source.place: Lemma 5.4.5.7; Proposition 5.3.3.3 for the finite homotopy-limit interchange

proof.text: Equivalences in the slice are detected on their source arrow: apply the pointwise equivalence criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] to the arrow category with fixed target; evaluation at the target is an isofibration by [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation], so [lem-coef-infinity-core-kan-fibration] makes its map of cores a Kan fibration. Its fiber over the target is Kan, hence contains inverses and inverse homotopies for all its edges. Thus the inverse of an equivalence triangle is available with target fixed. Finally the cone mapping-space fiber formula of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], for a singleton diagram, expresses each slice mapping space as a homotopy fiber of ambient mapping spaces. Small ambient mapping spaces have small path-space fibers, proving the slice local-smallness assertion.

source.place: Opposite of Lemma 5.4.5.4 for singleton diagrams; slice squares written out using the equivalence-arrow model

proof.text: For the slice assertion use the diagram identification in step 4 with $T\times\Delta^1$ and then fix the target diagram to be constant at $x=(a,b,e)$. A diagram in $\mathcal P_{/x}$ is a pair of diagrams of arrows $u:a_T\to a$, $v:b_T\to b$ and an equivalence $h:Fa_T\simeq Gb_T$ with a specified coherent square $eF(u)\simeq G(v)h$. Postcompose the second triangle by a coherent inverse of $e$. Here postcomposition is the coherent functor of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-slice-sections]: with $D=\mathcal C$ (replete), $K=\Delta^1$ and $p$ the edge $e^{-1}:G(b)\to F(a)$, respectively $e$, the cocartesian fibration $E_D\to\Delta^1$ has fibers the coherent slices $\mathcal C_{/G(b)}$, $\mathcal C_{/F(a)}$ and transport the postcomposition functor; its local-smallness hypothesis holds after enlarging the universe, which does not change the slices. Taking $K=\Delta^2$ and $p$ the two $2$-simplices witnessing $e^{-1}e\simeq1$ and $ee^{-1}\simeq1$, cocartesian edges over the three edges of $\Delta^2$ compose, so the composite transports are naturally equivalent to transport along an identity edge, which is the identity of the slice. The data become arrows $F(u):Fa_T\to F(a)$ and $e^{-1}G(v):Gb_T\to F(a)$ together with the equivalence $h$ between them in $\mathcal C_{/F(a)}$. Its higher simplices are exactly the same squares and higher compatibilities, with the two inverse-triangle homotopies for $e$ inserted. Conversely postcomposition by $e$ recovers the original data. The two composites are naturally equivalent to the identity by those same inverse-triangle homotopies. This construction commutes with simplicial restriction and thus gives the asserted coherent slice equivalence, not merely a bijection of objects. The fixed-target equivalence criterion in step 8 shows that the equivalence-arrow condition used here is exactly the one in the slice pullback. Full-subcategory restrictions retain exactly those simplices whose vertices satisfy the chosen conditions, so this construction restricts as claimed.

source.place: Opposite of Lemma 5.4.5.4 for singleton diagrams; slice squares written out using the equivalence-arrow model

proof.text: For full $\mathcal A',\mathcal B',\mathcal C'$, a simplex with vertices in $\mathcal P'$ projects to simplices in $\mathcal A',\mathcal B'$; its equivalence-arrow prism in $\mathcal C$ has all its vertices in $\mathcal C'$ and therefore belongs to $\mathcal C'$ by fullness. Conversely these three restricted data give exactly a simplex of $\mathcal P'$. Equivalence edges between objects of a full subcategory are the same as in the ambient category, since an inverse and its two witnessing triangles use only the same vertices. Thus $\mathcal P'$ is the strict equivalence-arrow model of the restricted homotopy pullback by step 2.

source.place: Full-subcategory and essential-smallness checks in Proposition 5.4.6.6, first paragraph; explicit small equivalence-arrow model

proof.text: For essential smallness choose small quasicategories $A_0,B_0,C_0$ equivalent to the three full subcategories, together with quasi-inverses and coherent comparison equivalences. Transport $F,G$ to $F_0:A_0\to C_0$, $G_0:B_0\to C_0$ by composition with these functors. The strict equivalence-arrow model $P_0'$ for this small cospan is small: in degree $n$ it is a subset of $(A_0)_n\times(B_0)_n\times\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta^n\times\Delta^1,C_0)$, a small set. To construct a coherent comparison functor, use the pullback universal property established in step 2, equivalently [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-pullback-limit], with test category $Q=P_0'$ in a larger universe. The component functors to $\mathcal A'$ and $\mathcal B'$ and the composite of the transported equivalence with the chosen natural comparison equivalences form a point of the homotopy pullback of functor cores. The universal-property equivalence supplies a functor $J:P_0'\to\mathcal P'$ representing that point, together with its coherent component comparisons.

source.place: Full-subcategory and essential-smallness checks in Proposition 5.4.6.6, first paragraph; explicit small equivalence-arrow model

proof.text: Step 3 shows $J$ is fully faithful because all three comparison functors induce equivalences on mapping spaces. For a triple $(a,b,e)$, choose $a_0,b_0$ and component equivalences to $a,b$. Full faithfulness of $C_0\to\mathcal C'$ lifts, up to a path in the relevant mapping space, the composite equivalence between $F_0(a_0)$ and $G_0(b_0)$ to an equivalence in $C_0$; it is an equivalence since a fully faithful functor reflects inverse edges and their witnessing triangles. These data give a triple of $P_0'$ whose image under $J$ is equivalent to $(a,b,e)$, by the specified comparison squares. Thus $J$ is essentially surjective. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image] to this fully faithful and essentially surjective functor: its full replete essential image is all of $\mathcal P'$, so it is an equivalence. This proves equivalence to an actual small quasicategory, rather than just smallness of the set of equivalence classes.
